article.deck: Visa trades 4.8% above the 385.67 buy point of a six-week flat base, at the top of a buy range that ends at 404.95.
body: Visa rose 1.77 to 404.02, up 0.4%, as of 1:38 p.m. Mountain, on a day the Nasdaq fell 5.2%. The stock sits 4.8% above the 385.67 buy point of a six-week flat base, 7.5% deep, and just under the 404.95 top of the buy range. It is on pace for 0.83x its 50-day average volume.

The breakout came Oct. 12 on 0.8x average volume. Since then the stock pulled back to the 50-day line, now 394.68, and bounced; it trades 2.4% above that line and 15.7% above the 200-day line at 349.17. The 21-day exponential line at 412.95 sits overhead: the session's high stayed 0.48 ATRs under it. The 52-week high is 442.23, 8.6% above the price. RS rank is 84 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is at a new high with the indexes sliding. The stock is up 15.2% this year and 24.7% over 12 months.

In the September quarter EPS rose 21.8% to 3.19 a share and revenue grew 13.2% to $12.139 billion. Revenue has climbed in each quarter in the table, from $10.901 billion in the December 2025 quarter to $11.23 billion, $11.633 billion and $12.139 billion. Next earnings are due Jan. 26, 2027. Market value is about $754 billion, with a forward P/E of 23.58.
Bloomberg reported that JPMorgan and Visa warned of a cyberattack that hit an outside vendor. The stock rose anyway.
A close back under the 50-day line at 394.68 would undo the bounce; a close above 404.95 takes the stock out of the buy range.
article.watch: Whether Visa can get back over the 21-day line at 412.95 or slips under the 50-day line at 394.68.

article.deck: Microsoft cleared a 553.82 deep-cup buy point Nov. 4 and now trades 12.6% below it and under its 50-day line; the entry is gone until a new base forms.
body: Microsoft fell 14.54 to 483.76, down 2.9%, as of 1:38 p.m. Mountain, on pace for 1.14x its 50-day average volume. The stock cleared the 553.82 buy point of a 51-week deep cup, 36.9% deep, on Nov. 4, trading 2.3x average volume that day. It now sits 12.6% below that buy point, a stalled breakout, well short of the 581.51 top of the buy range.

The selling has taken it under the 50-day line, now 519.82; the stock is 6.9% below that line and 6.6% below the 21-day exponential line at 518.0, with the session's high 0.87 ATRs under the 21-day line. It holds 9.0% above the 200-day line at 443.63. The stock is 13.5% off its 52-week high of 559.15, flat for the year and down 0.7% over 12 months. RS rank is 69 of 99 on the desk's list; the RS line is 4.7% below its high.

The quarters are not the problem. September-quarter EPS rose 32.3% to 4.92 a share and revenue grew 18.8% to $92.279 billion. Revenue rose in each quarter in the table, from $81.273 billion in the December 2025 quarter to $82.886 billion, $90.007 billion and $92.279 billion. Next earnings are due Jan. 27, 2027. Market value is about $3.6 trillion, with a forward P/E of 20.01.
Yahoo Finance asked in a video Friday whether Microsoft can catch up in the frontier AI race, and in another whether a handful of tech giants could control the future of AI.
A move back over the 50-day line at 519.82 would be the first repair; until then the buy point is history.
article.watch: Whether Microsoft holds the 200-day line at 443.63.

article.deck: Costco trades 2.2% past its 1096.60 cup buy point, inside a buy range that runs to 1151.43.
body: Costco Wholesale rose 26.46, or 2.4%, to 1120.29 as of 8:52 a.m. Mountain, pushing higher at the open while the Nasdaq fell 2.2%. The stock broke out on Nov. 13 from a 25-week cup that ran 19.5% deep from its May 19 high to its Sept. 25 low. The buy point is 1096.60 and the buy range runs to 1151.43; the stock sits 2.2% above the buy point, five sessions after the breakout. It is on pace for 1.85x its 50-day average volume. The breakout session traded 0.81x average.

The 52-week high is 1123.67, and the stock trades 0.3% below it. It sits 13.5% above its 50-day line at 987.09 and 1.94 ATRs from the 21-day line at 1062.27, a trend that is intact rather than stretched. Costco holds RS rank 91 of 99 on the desk's list, and its relative strength line is at a new high. The stock is up 29.9% this year and 25.8% over the past 12 months.

In the quarter ended Aug. 31, earnings rose 15.0% to 6.75 a share and revenue rose 11.1% to $95.72 billion. The three quarters before it printed EPS of 4.50, 4.58 and 4.93. The next report is due Dec. 10. The market values the company at $496.78 billion, 44.8 times forward earnings.
TheStreet reported Friday that Costco has a new member offer. Barron's reported that warehouse-club rival BJ's Wholesale beat on earnings with a $240 million wrinkle and that its stock was falling.
A close back under 1096.60 would turn the breakout into a stall.

body: Tesla fell 11.03, or 2.9%, to 363.38 as of 8:52 a.m. Mountain, extending its losses at the open and cutting below its 50-day line. The stock broke out Oct. 26 from a four-week flat base, 10.6% deep, on 1.42x its 50-day average volume. Nineteen sessions later it sits 6.1% below the 386.93 buy point, a stalled breakout. The base low is 345.88. The flat base formed after a bigger correction: Tesla remains below its Dec. 22, 2025 high of 498.83, which it fell from to a July 29 low of 297.38. The stock is 3.4% below its 50-day line at 375.99 and 4.8% below its 200-day line at 381.75. It trades 0.39 ATRs below the 21-day line at 380.04. Tesla is 27.2% off its 52-week high. In the September quarter, earnings fell 43.6% to 0.22 a share and revenue slipped 0.2% to $28.05 billion. EPS ran 0.24, 0.13 and 0.32 in the three quarters before. The next report is due Jan. 27. The market values Tesla at $1.44 trillion, 168.2 times forward earnings.

body: Intuit traded at 281.00 at 8:50 a.m. Eastern, down 29.02 or 9.4% from Thursday's close, after headlines said it lowered its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook and agreed to sell Mailchimp. The stock closed Thursday at 310.02, off 3.22 or 1.0%, on volume 1.34x its 50-day average. It sits in a 12-week cup, 29.7% deep, with a buy point of 373.08 and a buy range to 391.73. Thursday's close was 16.9% below the buy point. The cup formed after a much bigger correction, and the stock remains far below its 721.54 high from August 2025.

Nothing on this chart is buyable. Thursday's close sat 54.6% under the 52-week high of 682.27, 2.5% below the 50-day line at 317.91 and 10.9% below the 200-day at 347.87. It was 1.02 ATRs from the 21-day line at 331.57, on the underside. The early entry at the handle high of 351.49 from Nov. 16 is out of reach. Intuit is RS rank 25 of 99 on the desk's list, and the shares are down 53.2% this year and 52.3% over 12 months.

In the quarter ended July 31, earnings per share came to 1.34, down 0.7% from a year earlier, on revenue of $4.354 billion, up 13.7%. The table carries no year-over-year comparison for the earlier quarters. Nov. 19 was the listed earnings date; the figures from that report are not in the desk's data. Intuit has a market value of $82.85 billion and trades at 11.5 times forward earnings.

A Stocktwits headline said the stock drew multiple price target cuts after Intuit lowered its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook. Euronews reported that Bending Spoons will buy Mailchimp from Intuit in a $3.68 billion deal, and GuruFocus described the buyer as Berkshire-backed.
A move back over the 50-day line would be the first repair; until then this is a stock in a downtrend inside a base.
